# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

# - form all overlapping historical blocks whose following month is observed
# - exhaustive subset selection; for each subset fit nonnegative weights summing to one

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

from scipy.optimize import minimize

pids = sorted(df["period_id"].unique(), key=lambda x:int(x[1:]))
Y = np.array([[df[(df.band==b)&(df.period_id==p)]["mean_value"].iloc[0] for p in pids] for b in bands], dtype=float)
B,T = Y.shape

# Synthetic historical control choices:
# - use matching length m=3 and one forward month, giving 6 historical blocks
# - match all bands jointly
# - standardize each band over P01-P09 for fitting so high-variance indices do not dominate
# - nonnegative convex weights, selected exhaustively over all nonempty subsets
# - forecast is the weighted combination of the observed first forward months in raw units
m = 3
n = 1
target_idx = T - m  # recent matching window P07-P09 starts here (0-based index 6)
match_target_raw = Y[:, target_idx:target_idx+m]

mu = Y.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True)
sd = Y.std(axis=1, keepdims=True)
sd[sd == 0] = 1.0
Z = (Y - mu) / sd
match_target = Z[:, target_idx:target_idx+m].reshape(-1)

blocks = []
for s in range(0, T - m - n + 1):
    X = Z[:, s:s+m].reshape(-1)
    fwd_raw = Y[:, s+m]  # first forward month
    blocks.append((s, X, fwd_raw))

def fit_subset(idxs):
    Xmat = np.column_stack([blocks[i][1] for i in idxs])
    k = len(idxs)
    if k == 1:
        w = np.ones(1)
        pred = Xmat[:,0]
        mse = float(np.mean((pred - match_target)**2))
        return mse, w
    def obj(w):
        r = Xmat @ w - match_target
        return float(np.mean(r*r))
    cons = {"type":"eq", "fun":lambda w: np.sum(w)-1.0}
    bounds = [(0.0,1.0)]*k
    res = minimize(obj, np.ones(k)/k, method="SLSQP", bounds=bounds, constraints=cons,
                   options={"ftol":1e-12, "maxiter":1000, "disp":False})
    w = res.x if res.success else np.ones(k)/k
    w = np.clip(w,0,None)
    if w.sum() == 0: w[:] = 1.0/k
    w = w/w.sum()
    return obj(w), w

best = None
for r in range(1, len(blocks)+1):
    for idxs in itertools.combinations(range(len(blocks)), r):

        score = mse + 1e-10*r

The parcel's past is its comparison: blocks of its own earlier months are weighted to

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

bands=list(df['band'].drop_duplicates())
periods=sorted(df['period_id'].unique(), key=lambda x:int(x[1:]))
Y=np.array([[df[(df.band==b)&(df.period_id==p)].mean_value.iloc[0] for p in periods] for b in bands],float)

# Prepare series: standardize each band so high-magnitude indices do not dominate.
# With only nine months and a sharp recent vegetation regime, use raw standardized
# observations rather than estimating a seasonal cycle from <1 year.
mu=Y.mean(axis=1,keepdims=True); sd=Y.std(axis=1,keepdims=True); sd[sd==0]=1
Z=(Y-mu)/sd

m=3; n=1
T=Z.shape[1]
starts=list(range(0,T-m-n+1)) # blocks matching starts
match_start=T-m
target=Z[:,match_start:T].reshape(-1)

X=[]
F=[]
for s in starts:
    X.append(Z[:,s:s+m].reshape(-1))
    F.append(Y[:,s+m]) # observed first forward month in original scale
X=np.array(X).T
F=np.array(F).T
K=len(starts)

def fit_subset(sub):
    sub=list(sub)
    A=X[:,sub]
    k=len(sub)
    if k==1:
        w=np.ones(1)
    else:
        def obj(w):
            r=A@w-target
            return float(np.mean(r*r))
        cons=({'type':'eq','fun':lambda w: np.sum(w)-1},)
        bnds=[(0,1)]*k
        x0=np.ones(k)/k
        res=minimize(obj,x0,method='SLSQP',bounds=bnds,constraints=cons,
                     options={'ftol':1e-12,'maxiter':1000, 'disp':False})
        w=res.x if res.success else x0
        w=np.clip(w,0,None); w=w/w.sum() if w.sum()>0 else np.ones(k)/k
    err=np.mean((A@w-target)**2)
    return err,w

# Exhaustive subset selection with a small parsimony tolerance: among fits within
# 2% of the best MSE, choose the smallest subset, then the lowest MSE. This avoids
# arbitrary overfitting while retaining the synthetic-control construction.
cands=[]
for r in range(1,K+1):
    for sub in itertools.combinations(range(K),r):
        err,w=fit_subset(sub)
        cands.append((err,r,sub,w))

# Implement and run the synthetic historical control

The parcel's past is its comparison: blocks of its own earlier months are weighted to
reproduce its most recent months, and what followed those blocks becomes the forecast.
`references/method.md` describes the construction; every setting and every choice in it
is yours, made inside your program.

## Workflow

1. `python scripts/show_data.py` — the nine months, every band. The same data is in
   `data.csv` in this directory: one row per band per month, columns `band`, `period_id`
   (P01–P09 in time order), `month` (YYYY-MM), `mean_value`.
2. Read `references/method.md`. Decide how to build the blocks, what to match, how to fit
   and constrain the weights, how to select blocks, and how to form the prediction.

   predicted mean value for the next month. numpy, scipy and pandas are available; nothing
   outside this directory is, and there is no network.
4. Run `python predict.py`. Fix what fails; run again. Every run is recorded.

   ```json

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

import json
import itertools
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy.optimize import minimize

df = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
bands = list(df["band"].drop_duplicates())
periods = sorted(df["period_id"].unique(), key=lambda x:int(x[1:]))
Y = np.array([[df[(df.band==b)&(df.period_id==p)]["mean_value"].iloc[0] for p in periods] for b in bands], float)

# Preparation: standardize each band so high-magnitude indices and reflectances contribute comparably.
mu = Y.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True)
sd = Y.std(axis=1, ddof=0, keepdims=True)
Z = (Y - mu) / sd

def fit_subset(X, y, subset):
    # X columns are candidate historical blocks flattened over band x time.
    A = X[:, subset]
    k = len(subset)
    if k == 1:
        w = np.array([1.0])
    else:
        def obj(w):
            r = A @ w - y
            return float(np.mean(r*r))
        cons = [{"type":"eq", "fun":lambda w: np.sum(w)-1.0}]
        bounds = [(0.0,1.0)]*k
        x0 = np.ones(k)/k
        res = minimize(obj, x0, method="SLSQP", bounds=bounds, constraints=cons,
                       options={"ftol":1e-12, "maxiter":1000, "disp":False})
        w = res.x if res.success else x0
        w = np.clip(w,0,None)
        w = w/w.sum() if w.sum()>0 else x0
    err = np.mean((A @ w - y)**2)
    full = np.zeros(X.shape[1])
    for idx, wi in zip(subset, w):
        full[idx] = wi
    return err, full

def shc_predict(m=3, tol=1e-4):
    nblocks = 9 - m  # one forward month
    # candidate match blocks: starts 0..nblocks-1, each m months
    X = np.column_stack([Z[:, s:s+m].reshape(-1) for s in range(nblocks)])
    target = Z[:, 9-m:9].reshape(-1)
    # stepwise selection: single best, then add only if MSE improvement exceeds tol fraction
    best_err = np.inf; selected = None; weights = None
    for j in range(nblocks):
        err, w = fit_subset(X, target, [j])
        if err < best_err:
            best_err, selected, weights = err, [j], w
    while True:
        cand_best = (best_err, selected, weights)
        for j in range(nblocks):
            if j in selected: continue
            subset = selected + [j]
            err, w = fit_subset(X, target, subset)
            if err < cand_best[0]:
                cand_best = (err, subset, w)
        improvement = best_err - cand_best[0]
        if improvement > tol * max(best_err, 1e-12):
            best_err, selected, weights = cand_best
        else:
            break
    # weighted first forward month after each block, undo standardization
    fwdZ = np.column_stack([Z[:, s+m] for s in range(nblocks)])
    predZ = fwdZ @ weights
    pred = (predZ.reshape(-1,1) * sd + mu).ravel()
    return pred, selected, weights, best_err

pred, selected, weights, err = shc_predict(m=3, tol=1e-4)

# keep physically/index plausible broad bounds by historical min/max expanded a little
mins, maxs = Y.min(axis=1), Y.max(axis=1)
rng = maxs - mins
pred = np.minimum(np.maximum(pred, mins - 0.25*rng), maxs + 0.25*rng)

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.
